Ollama Setup Guide

Start the Ollama service and pick a small local chat model. Run one short prompt, then check that the same server reports the model in ollama ps. Once local chat works, choose the next task: connect an app, verify GPU and context, or search your own documents.

  1. Start and verify local chat
  2. Check your Ollama setup
  3. Continue with your task

Start with one local model

Install Ollama for your operating system from the official download page. Open the app, or start ollama serve if you installed the CLI and no Ollama service is already running. Run these commands from a second terminal if the first is running the server:

ollama --version
ollama list
ollama run qwen2.5:0.5b "Reply with exactly LOCAL_OK."
ollama ps

The example downloads a small model if it is missing. An assistant reply confirms a prompt completed. The exact tag in ollama ps confirms it is loaded on the server the CLI is using. Check promptly because the model can unload after a timeout. For a first run on Apple Silicon, follow the full Mac setup and loopback test.

Check the server, model list and endpoints

Download the Python check and run it with Python 3.9 or newer. By default it reads the version and two model lists on 127.0.0.1:11434. It uses the standard library, skips HTTP proxies and makes no model downloads. If you run Ollama on a different local port, pass the actual port with --port.

python3 check-ollama.py

An empty model list with a valid version means the server responded. If there is no version, check that the app or service is running on the expected port. A missing /v1/models response affects clients using the OpenAI-compatible route, even when the native list works. Troubleshoot connection, missing models and HTTP 404.

To exercise inference, copy the exact tags returned under native_model_tags. Pass either model flag by itself or both flags together. The example assumes those tags are already installed. These optional checks send a short synthetic chat prompt and two synthetic texts.

python3 check-ollama.py --chat-model qwen2.5:0.5b --embedding-model nomic-embed-text:v1.5

On one Apple M4 with Ollama 0.40.18, both installed test tags appeared in both lists. The chat request finished with LOCAL_OK and the embedding request returned two 768-dimensional vectors. A deliberately missing chat tag failed its check while embeddings still passed. After stopping the test service, the version check failed. Download all four test results.

Continue with your task

Return JSON matching a schema
Check the response shape, finish reason and extracted values.
Connect an OpenAI SDK client
Use the local /v1/ base URL and distinguish the two tested kinds of 404.
Use the model in OpenCode
Verify that the same model appears in OpenCode and answers a bounded request.
Check GPU placement or verify context length
Read the loaded model’s processor and context before changing its settings.
Extract a PDF with MarkItDown and rank pages with Ollama embeddings
Check whether retrieved text actually contains the answer, including text recovered by OCR.
Update an installed model
Pull the exact library tag and keep a local copy for rollback.
Find or move the model store
Copy the full Ollama models folder and check that your tags still load.
Unload or delete a model
Check the running list or the disk store, depending on which space you need.

See Ollama’s CLI reference and API reference for other commands and endpoints.
